_comment: Armour plate materials. The quality factor scales a plate's resistance relative to US Class A, which is used as the reference at 1.00. These figures are the most contested numbers in the whole data set: wartime and post-war assessments disagree, national test methods differed, and plate quality varied between batches within a single navy. They are here, tunable, and marked with confidence for exactly that reason.
_faceHardenedComment: Face-hardened plate has a hard outer layer over a tough backing. It is markedly better against uncapped shells, which it tends to shatter, and markedly worse against a capped shell that can punch the hard face through. Homogeneous plate has no such asymmetry and is what decks, bulkheads and torpedo protection are made of.

usa_class_a.name: US Class A (face-hardened)
usa_class_a.notes: The reference against which the other factors here are expressed.

usa_sts.name: US Special Treatment Steel
usa_sts.notes: Structural steel good enough to count as protection. Used for splinter decks, plating and the backing behind Class A.

uk_d_steel.name: British D Quality Steel
uk_d_steel.notes: Structural rather than armour grade; the splinter plating destroyers were given.

ger_wh.name: Wotan Hart (homogeneous)
ger_wh.notes: Used for decks and torpedo bulkheads. Wotan Weich, a softer grade, was used where ductility mattered more than hardness.

jpn_vh.name: Vickers Hardened
jpn_vh.notes: Post-war US testing of Japanese plate suggested it was somewhat inferior to Western face-hardened armour, particularly in the very thick sections used on Yamato. The size of that penalty is genuinely disputed; this factor is a reasonable middle estimate and is the first number to revisit if Yamato feels wrong.

jpn_ds.name: Ducol Steel
jpn_ds.notes: High-tensile structural steel used for splinter protection and light plating.

generic_homogeneous.name: Generic homogeneous armour
generic_homogeneous.notes: Default for custom designs in the ship designer, and the fallback when a plate names a material that is not defined.

structural_steel.name: Mild structural steel
structural_steel.notes: Ordinary shell plating and bulkheads. Barely resists a shell at all, but it is what stops splinters and what floods when it is holed, so it has to be modelled as structure rather than ignored.
